questions.question: What is TypeScript?
questions.answer: TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that adds static type checking. It compiles to plain JavaScript and helps catch errors at compile time.

questions.question: What are the basic types in TypeScript?
questions.answer: Basic types include: string, number, boolean, null, undefined, any, unknown, never, and void. TypeScript also supports arrays, tuples, and enums.

questions.question: What is an interface in TypeScript?
questions.answer: An interface defines a contract for the structure of an object. It specifies what properties and methods an object must have, but doesn't provide implementation.

questions.question: What are generics in TypeScript?
questions.answer: Generics allow you to create reusable components that work with multiple types. They use type variables (like <T>) to define flexible, type-safe functions and classes.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'any' and 'unknown'?
questions.answer: 'any' disables type checking, while 'unknown' is type-safe and requires type checking before use. 'unknown' is preferred for safety.

questions.question: What is a type alias?
questions.answer: A type alias creates a new name for any type using the 'type' keyword. It can represent primitives, unions, tuples, and any other types.

questions.question: What are utility types in TypeScript?
questions.answer: Utility types are built-in types that help transform other types. Examples include Partial, Required, Readonly, Pick, Omit, and Record.

questions.question: What are access modifiers in TypeScript?
questions.answer: Access modifiers (public, private, protected) control the visibility of class members. public is default, private restricts access, protected allows subclass access.

questions.question: What is a union type?
questions.answer: A union type allows a value to be one of several types. It's defined using the | operator, e.g., string | number allows either a string or number.

questions.question: What is type narrowing?
questions.answer: Type narrowing is the process of refining a variable's type within a code block. It uses techniques like typeof, instanceof, and type guards.

questions.question: What is an enum in TypeScript?
questions.answer: An enum is a way to define a set of named constants. Enums can be numeric (default) or string-based and provide meaningful names for values.

questions.question: What is a mapped type?
questions.answer: A mapped type creates a new type by transforming properties of an existing type. It uses the 'in' keyword to iterate over properties dynamically.

questions.question: What is a tuple type?
questions.answer: A tuple type is an array with a fixed number of elements of specific types. For example, [string, number] is a tuple with a string and number.

questions.question: What is the void type?
questions.answer: The void type represents the absence of a value. It's commonly used for functions that don't return anything.

questions.question: What is the never type?
questions.answer: The never type represents a value that never occurs. It's used for functions that never return or always throw errors.

questions.question: What is an intersection type?
questions.answer: An intersection type combines multiple types using the & operator. It represents an object with all properties from all types.

questions.question: What is a literal type?
questions.answer: A literal type is a specific value of a type. For example, 'hello' is a literal type that only accepts the string 'hello'.

questions.question: What is a conditional type?
questions.answer: A conditional type selects one of two types based on a condition. It uses the ternary operator syntax: T extends U ? X : Y.

questions.question: What is a class in TypeScript?
questions.answer: A class is a blueprint for creating objects. It defines properties, methods, and constructors with type annotations.

questions.question: What is a constructor in TypeScript?
questions.answer: A constructor is a special method called when creating a class instance. It initializes properties and can accept parameters.

questions.question: What is inheritance in TypeScript?
questions.answer: Inheritance allows a class to extend another class using the 'extends' keyword. The child class inherits properties and methods from the parent.

questions.question: What is an abstract class?
questions.answer: An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly. It serves as a base class for other classes and can contain abstract methods.

questions.question: What is an abstract method?
questions.answer: An abstract method is declared but not implemented in an abstract class. Subclasses must implement abstract methods.

questions.question: What is a static member?
questions.answer: A static member belongs to the class itself, not to instances. It's accessed using the class name, not an instance.

questions.question: What is a getter and setter?
questions.answer: Getters and setters are special methods for accessing and modifying properties. They allow custom logic when getting or setting values.

questions.question: What is a type guard?
questions.answer: A type guard is a function that checks if a value is of a specific type. It narrows the type within a conditional block.

questions.question: What is the 'is' keyword?
questions.answer: The 'is' keyword is used in type guard functions to assert a type. It helps TypeScript understand type narrowing.

questions.question: What is the 'as' keyword?
questions.answer: The 'as' keyword performs type assertion. It tells TypeScript to treat a value as a specific type.

questions.question: What is the 'keyof' operator?
questions.answer: The 'keyof' operator gets the union of all property names of a type. It's useful for creating type-safe property accessors.

questions.question: What is the 'typeof' operator?
questions.answer: The 'typeof' operator gets the type of a value. It's useful for type narrowing and creating types from values.

questions.question: What is the 'instanceof' operator?
questions.answer: The 'instanceof' operator checks if an object is an instance of a class. It's useful for type narrowing.

questions.question: What is the 'in' operator?
questions.answer: The 'in' operator checks if a property exists in an object. It's useful for type narrowing and property checking.

questions.question: What is the 'readonly' modifier?
questions.answer: The 'readonly' modifier prevents modification of a property after initialization. It's useful for immutability.

questions.question: What is the 'optional' property?
questions.answer: An optional property is marked with '?' and may or may not exist. For example, name?: string means name is optional.

questions.question: What is the 'required' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'Required' utility type makes all properties of a type required. It removes optional markers from properties.

questions.question: What is the 'partial' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'Partial' utility type makes all properties of a type optional. It adds optional markers to all properties.

questions.question: What is the 'readonly' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'Readonly' utility type makes all properties of a type readonly. It prevents modification of properties.

questions.question: What is the 'pick' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'Pick' utility type selects specific properties from a type. For example, Pick<User, 'name' | 'email'> creates a type with only name and email.

questions.question: What is the 'omit' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'Omit' utility type excludes specific properties from a type. For example, Omit<User, 'password'> creates a type without password.

questions.question: What is the 'record' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'Record' utility type creates a type with specific keys and values. For example, Record<'a' | 'b', string> creates {a: string, b: string}.

questions.question: What is the 'exclude' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'Exclude' utility type removes types from a union. For example, Exclude<'a' | 'b' | 'c', 'a'> results in 'b' | 'c'.

questions.question: What is the 'extract' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'Extract' utility type keeps only types that match a condition in a union. For example, Extract<'a' | 'b' | 'c', 'a' | 'b'> results in 'a' | 'b'.

questions.question: What is the 'nonnullable' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'NonNullable' utility type removes null and undefined from a type. For example, NonNullable<string | null> results in string.

questions.question: What is the 'parameters' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'Parameters' utility type extracts parameter types from a function type. It's useful for getting function parameter types.

questions.question: What is the 'returntype' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'ReturnType' utility type extracts the return type from a function type. It's useful for getting function return types.

questions.question: What is the 'awaited' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'Awaited' utility type unwraps Promise types. For example, Awaited<Promise<string>> results in string.

questions.question: What is the 'thisparametertype' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'ThisParameterType' utility type extracts the 'this' parameter type from a function. It's useful for understanding function context.

questions.question: What is the 'omitthiscontext' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'OmitThisContext' utility type removes the 'this' parameter from a function type. It's useful for removing context requirements.

questions.question: What is the 'thistype' utility type?
questions.answer: The 'ThisType' utility type specifies the 'this' context for an object. It's useful for method definitions.

questions.question: What is the 'intrinsic' keyword?
questions.answer: The 'intrinsic' keyword is used for special utility types. It's used internally by TypeScript for built-in transformations.

questions.question: What is a decorator?
questions.answer: A decorator is a function that modifies a class, method, or property. It's useful for adding metadata and cross-cutting concerns.

questions.question: What is a class decorator?
questions.answer: A class decorator is applied to a class. It can modify the class or its constructor.

questions.question: What is a method decorator?
questions.answer: A method decorator is applied to a method. It can modify the method or its behavior.

questions.question: What is a property decorator?
questions.answer: A property decorator is applied to a property. It can modify the property or its descriptor.

questions.question: What is a parameter decorator?
questions.answer: A parameter decorator is applied to a function parameter. It can access metadata about the parameter.

questions.question: What is metadata reflection?
questions.answer: Metadata reflection allows storing and retrieving metadata about types at runtime. It's useful for dependency injection and serialization.

questions.question: What is the reflect-metadata library?
questions.answer: reflect-metadata is a library that provides metadata reflection APIs. It's required for using decorators with metadata.

questions.question: What is a module in TypeScript?
questions.answer: A module is a file that exports and imports code. TypeScript supports ES6 modules and CommonJS modules.

questions.question: What is the 'export' keyword?
questions.answer: The 'export' keyword makes a variable, function, or class available for import in other modules.

questions.question: What is the 'import' keyword?
questions.answer: The 'import' keyword imports exported members from other modules. It can import specific members or entire modules.

questions.question: What is a namespace?
questions.answer: A namespace is a way to organize code and avoid naming conflicts. It's an older way to organize code, modules are preferred.

questions.question: What is the 'declare' keyword?
questions.answer: The 'declare' keyword declares a variable, function, or class without implementation. It's useful for type definitions.

questions.question: What is a type definition file?
questions.answer: A type definition file (.d.ts) contains type information for JavaScript libraries. It allows using JavaScript libraries with type safety.

questions.question: What is DefinitelyTyped?
questions.answer: DefinitelyTyped is a repository of type definitions for JavaScript libraries. It provides @types packages for popular libraries.

questions.question: What is the 'tsconfig.json' file?
questions.answer: tsconfig.json is the configuration file for TypeScript. It specifies compiler options and project settings.

questions.question: What is the 'target' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'target' option specifies the JavaScript version to compile to. Common values are ES5, ES6, ES2020, etc.

questions.question: What is the 'module' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'module' option specifies the module system to use. Common values are commonjs, es6, esnext, etc.

questions.question: What is the 'strict' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'strict' option enables all strict type checking options. It's recommended for better type safety.

questions.question: What is the 'noImplicitAny' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'noImplicitAny' option prevents implicit any types. It requires explicit type annotations.

questions.question: What is the 'strictNullChecks' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'strictNullChecks' option treats null and undefined as distinct types. It prevents null reference errors.

questions.question: What is the 'strictFunctionTypes' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'strictFunctionTypes' option enforces stricter function type checking. It prevents unsafe function assignments.

questions.question: What is the 'strictBindCallApply' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'strictBindCallApply' option enforces stricter bind, call, and apply checking. It prevents unsafe method calls.

questions.question: What is the 'strictPropertyInitialization' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'strictPropertyInitialization' option requires properties to be initialized. It prevents undefined properties.

questions.question: What is the 'noImplicitThis' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'noImplicitThis' option prevents implicit any for 'this'. It requires explicit 'this' types.

questions.question: What is the 'alwaysStrict' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'alwaysStrict' option adds 'use strict' to all files. It enables strict mode in all modules.

questions.question: What is the 'noUnusedLocals' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'noUnusedLocals' option reports errors on unused local variables. It helps clean up code.

questions.question: What is the 'noUnusedParameters' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'noUnusedParameters' option reports errors on unused parameters. It helps clean up function signatures.

questions.question: What is the 'noImplicitReturns' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'noImplicitReturns' option requires all code paths to return a value. It prevents missing return statements.

questions.question: What is the 'noFallthroughCasesInSwitch' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'noFallthroughCasesInSwitch' option prevents fallthrough in switch statements. It requires break or return in each case.

questions.question: What is the 'esModuleInterop' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'esModuleInterop' option enables interoperability between ES modules and CommonJS. It allows importing CommonJS modules as ES modules.

questions.question: What is the 'allowSyntheticDefaultImports' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'allowSyntheticDefaultImports' option allows importing default exports from modules without default exports. It's useful for CommonJS compatibility.

questions.question: What is the 'forceConsistentCasingInFileNames' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'forceConsistentCasingInFileNames' option enforces consistent casing in file names. It prevents case-sensitivity issues.

questions.question: What is the 'declaration' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'declaration' option generates .d.ts files for type definitions. It's useful for publishing libraries.

questions.question: What is the 'declarationMap' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'declarationMap' option generates source maps for .d.ts files. It helps with debugging type definitions.

questions.question: What is the 'sourceMap' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'sourceMap' option generates source maps for JavaScript files. It helps with debugging compiled code.

questions.question: What is the 'outDir' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'outDir' option specifies the output directory for compiled files. It's useful for organizing build output.

questions.question: What is the 'rootDir' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'rootDir' option specifies the root directory of source files. It's used to determine the output directory structure.

questions.question: What is the 'baseUrl' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'baseUrl' option specifies the base directory for module resolution. It's useful for absolute imports.

questions.question: What is the 'paths' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'paths' option specifies path mappings for module resolution. It's useful for creating aliases for imports.

questions.question: What is the 'skipLibCheck' compiler option?
questions.answer: The 'skipLibCheck' option skips type checking of declaration files. It speeds up compilation.

questions.question: What is the difference between interface and type?
questions.answer: Interfaces define object shapes and can be extended. Types are more flexible and can represent any type. Use interfaces for object shapes, types for unions and primitives.

questions.question: What is the difference between class and interface?
questions.answer: Classes provide implementation and can be instantiated. Interfaces only define contracts. Classes can implement interfaces.

questions.question: What is the difference between any and unknown?
questions.answer: 'any' disables type checking completely. 'unknown' requires type checking before use. 'unknown' is safer.

questions.question: What is the difference between never and void?
questions.answer: 'void' means no return value. 'never' means the function never returns (infinite loop or throws error).

questions.question: What is the difference between union and intersection types?
questions.answer: Union types (|) allow one of several types. Intersection types (&) combine all types together.

questions.question: What is the difference between type and interface for functions?
questions.answer: Types can represent function signatures directly. Interfaces require a call signature. Both work, but types are more concise.

questions.question: What is the difference between const and readonly?
questions.answer: 'const' prevents reassignment of variables. 'readonly' prevents modification of object properties.

questions.question: What is the difference between extends and implements?
questions.answer: 'extends' creates inheritance from a class or interface. 'implements' ensures a class conforms to an interface.

questions.question: What is the difference between public and protected?
questions.answer: 'public' members are accessible everywhere. 'protected' members are accessible in the class and subclasses.

questions.question: What is the difference between TypeScript and JavaScript?
questions.answer: TypeScript adds static type checking to JavaScript. It compiles to JavaScript and provides better tooling and error detection.
